title: Launch Ops Sprint Canvas + Shoulder-Tap Matrix
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact sprint canvas intended for short-run launch cycles (2–3 weeks) where product-ops needs a single-pane operational readiness snapshot + escalation/"shoulder-tap" matrix. The goal: reduce ambiguity at T-72h and make quick decisions on scope/traffic gating.

When to use:
- Small feature launches with ML inference surface changes (model swap, quantization change, routing policy tweaks)
- Beta to limited audiences and staged rollouts to Dedicated accounts
- Any rollout where latency/cost KPIs could drive immediate rollback decisions

Top-level executive snapshot (one line each):
- Launch name: SmartSuggest v2 limited beta
- Sprint window: 2024-12-10 -> 2024-12-21
- Primary owners: Product (Sana Iqbal), Product-Ops (Asha Patel), SRE (Jonah Reed)
- Canary cohort: 5% of web traffic, select enterprise beta orgs

Sprint canvas (quick fields):
- Outcome hypothesis: Increase suggestion relevance (CTR↑ 8ppt) while keeping median serving latency ≤ 150ms and token cost change ≤ +12%.
- Must-have acceptance (go/no-go): no more than 1% increase in P95 error rate for inference calls; no SLO breach on 2 consecutive hours in canary window.
- Nice-to-have: telemetry on prompt-variation segmentation and improved developer debug traces for failed generations.
- Key KPIs (baseline -> target):
  * Median latency (A): 120ms -> <=150ms
  * P95 latency (B): 260ms -> <=300ms
  * Production CTR (relevance) (C): 18% -> +8ppt
  * Per-request token cost (D): $0.045 -> <= $0.050
  * Error rate (E): 0.6% -> <=1.0%

Owners and immediate tasks (T-14 -> T-0):
- Product-Ops (Asha): compile readiness pack T-7; run smoke on staging T-5; coordinate on-call rotations T-2
- SRE (Jonah): capacity check and canary routing rules T-10; define fallback policy T-3
- Serving-runtime (Miguel): validation run of quantized model on representative batch T-6; perf profiler attached T-4
- Observability (Sana / analytics): wire feature flags to dashboards T-5; add segment sampling T-3

Traffic & capacity guardrails (quick table):
- Canary step 1: 1% global, 60m observation
- Canary step 2: 5% global, 3h observation
- Ramp step: 20% and pause for 12h telemetry review
- Burst allowance: up to +2x baseline QPS for 10 minutes with automatic fallback

Decision thresholds (automated overrides):
- If P95 latency > 350ms for 30 minutes -> automatic throttle to previous model variant and notify SRE + Product-Ops
- If error rate > 2.0% in any cohort -> abort ramp, rollback to prior model, open incident channel
- If per-request cost increase > 20% sustained for 1 hour and usage growth does not explain it -> pause rollout and escalate to finance (Miguel)

Shoulder-tap escalation matrix (who to call in-band + out-of-band):
- Severity: S1 (systemic outage affecting canary or >10% of canary users) -> Pager: SRE oncall (Jonah Reed), Shoulder-tap: Head of SRE (Priya Kumar), Product lead (Sana)
- Severity: S2 (latency or quality regressions but not widespread) -> Shoulder-tap: Product-Ops (Asha), Observability lead (Miguel)
- Severity: S3 (cost anomalies or single-tenant failures) -> Shoulder-tap: Finance-signal (Ravi Shah), Solutions Eng rep for tenant

Communication plan:
- T-24: activation email to #launch-ops with links to readiness pack and dashboards
- During canary: live updates every 60–120 minutes in #launch-ops; status emoji on spreadsheet
- Post-rollout: 1-hour debrief + 72h follow-up evaluation against KPIs

Quick-run checklist (T-3 to T+1):
- T-3: Validate infra runbook exists and oncall rota published (owner: Product-Ops)
- T-2: Confirm traffic routing rules and rollback playbook are tested on staging (owner: SRE)
- T-1: Verify real telemetry (latency/cost/kpi) shows expected baseline in a synthetic load run (owner: Serving-runtime)
- T-0 hour: Flip feature-flag to 1% then observe for 60m (owner: Product-Ops)
- T+0.5h: Fill short-form incident log entry if any anomaly (owner: oncall SRE)
- T+24h: Postmortem or minor retrospective capture in confluence ticket

Lightweight risk register (top 5):
1) Model quantization introduces rare hallucination patterns -> mitigation: limited cohort + manual review queue
2) Autoscaling lag under spiky traffic -> mitigation: temporary buffer nodes and burst policy in router
3) Observability sampling misses cohort -> mitigation: ensure 100% trace sampling for canary tenants in first 3h
4) Unexpected token cost delta -> mitigation: cost sentinel alert and finance shoulder-tap
5) Customer-facing regressions in enterprise tenant -> mitigation: immediate holdback and direct SE outreach

Notes, ask list and unresolved items:
- Need final signoff from Legal for enterprise beta T-4 (assigned to Sana)
- Confirm billing tags propagated to logs for accurate per-request cost attribution (assigned to Miguel)
- Open question: allow X% of retries in router vs drop? default suggestion: 1 retry for idempotent requests only.

Appendix (quick links):
- Readiness pack (confluence): confluence:PRODOPS-Launch-Central-5478
- Canary runbook (doc): confluence:Canary-Runbook-2024
- Incident template: confluence:Incident-Template-OPS

Usage notes: keep this file as the sprint-level single source of truth for all operational decisions during the launch window. Link to more detailed trackers (capacity spreadsheets, SLO dashboards) rather than copying them. Update the Status line at top on each major change (e.g., "T-2: green; T-1: amber").

Last updated by: Asha Patel (product-ops) — 2024-12-15
